title: ephor project manifest (ephor.json)
description: What a project may offer ephor, placed as 'ephor.json' at the forest root (FS-006-project-interface.2). Offered, never required: every field is optional, an empty object is valid, and nothing here gates a capability that probing or site configuration could not establish alone. Resolution is always site configuration over manifest over probe (REQ-001-boundary.2). Identity fields are hints the registry row adopts unless it overrides — the row is authoritative. Commands run relative to the forest root with the trust the person extends to the project's own build; the row's trust switch can narrow this to descriptions only.

identity.description: Hints for attribution (FS-008-attribution.1). Of these, aliases, territory, addresses and rooms are adopted, each only where the registry row writes no list of that name, never overriding it (FS-008-attribution.1.1); name, ticket_patterns and repos are not read as identity.

ticket_patterns.description: Regular expressions matching the project's ticket keys, e.g. 'GR-\\d+'.

repos.description: The forest's repositories as the forge names them (owner/name or slug).

territory.description: Repositories and organizations that are this project's business without being in its forest — 'owner/name', or 'owner/*' for an organization. Places general mentions, stray issues, adjacent discussions (FS-008-attribution.1).

addresses.description: Mail addresses and lists whose conversations belong to this project.

rooms.description: Rooms on a conversation source whose conversations belong to this project, each the id the source states (FS-008-attribution.1). A hint: adopted only where the registry row says nothing about rooms, so a row listing none refuses it.

main.description: The main branch this repository trails (default: the project's).

forest.description: The forest's own layout (AR-004-forest). The registry row overrides paths and remotes for where things sit on a particular machine.

checks.description: Check verbs (FS-006-project-interface.5), overriding the probed ./check.sh, ./check-style.sh, ./smoke-test.sh. Each script is self-contained: a smoke test that needs a build performs its build.

oneOf.description: Discover by running the command with --list; it prints one feature id per line, or a features[] envelope.

clean.description: The clean verb (FS-017-clean.1), overriding the probed ./clean.sh: what gives back the space the project's builds took in one checkout, run there by `ephor clean`. Beside `checks` rather than in it, because a project that can clean is not thereby checkable.

ci.description: Gate verbs (FS-006-project-interface.6) — project truth, the same for every developer; site configuration overrides for credentials or variants. Each is a summons: EPHOR_* environment in (EPHOR_REPO, EPHOR_NUMBER, EPHOR_BRANCH name the matter), exit code plus $EPHOR_ANSWER envelope out. status answers gate; failures answers failures[]; restart re-runs the failing gate and everything downstream of it, committing nothing (FS-005-dispatch.11), exit 75 meaning 'still running, ask again later'.

tasks.description: The project's own task stores beyond the probed conventions (FS-006-project-interface.7). These are the project's own work, kept in its own checkout: a ticket is what a remote tracker keys and an issue is what a forge files, and neither is this.

tickets.description: The older spelling of 'tasks', still read (FS-006-project-interface.11). Prefer 'tasks'.

actions.description: The project's offers (FS-006-project-interface.9): menu entries beside the person's own, person's same-id entries winning. Invoked by a person, run as a summons, gated by 'requires'.

items.description: One monitor's declaration. Any entry is accepted here so that one declaration ephor cannot use costs that monitor alone: ephor checks each entry on its own against $defs/monitor, and one that fails is shown with what is wrong and not read, while the manifest's other monitors, checks, offers and task stores are read as usual. 'ephor validate --manifest' holds every entry to $defs/monitor and refuses the manifest, naming each that fails (FS-021-monitors.4.6).

monitors.description: Quantities the project asks ephor to read at their own cadence, keep as history and draw (FS-021-monitors.4.1). A monitor something judges is a status, and its drop is a matter; one nothing judges is a KPI (FS-021-monitors.1.2). Site configuration overrides any field by naming the id (FS-021-monitors.4.4). Rules that join two fields (a warn laxer than healthy, an 'at' that does not fit 'every', an id declared twice) are judged per monitor too, and cost that monitor alone (FS-021-monitors.4.6).

monitor.description: One monitor's declaration, the shape each entry of 'monitors' is checked against, in the manifest and in site configuration alike (FS-021-monitors.4.1, FS-021-monitors.4.2). Only 'id' is required; a title defaults to the id. The site may write null for 'warn', 'at', 'from', 'workflow' or 'action' to set aside what the manifest says (FS-021-monitors.4.4).

description.description: One line saying what the number is for.

better.description: Which direction is better; colours a change and says which way is worse (FS-021-monitors.2.2).

of.description: The whole the value is a fraction of, shown as '12/15'. A sample's own 'of' is that reading's, and this stands where a sample states none (FS-021-monitors.2.2).

healthy.description: The condition (FS-021-monitors.3.1), taken whole from the home that names it. Absent from every home, a boolean is healthy when true and a level at its first level, and a number or a series is judged by its samples' own ok where they state one and is a KPI otherwise; null makes any monitor a KPI whatever its samples say (FS-021-monitors.3.2, FS-021-monitors.3.6).

warn.description: A second condition a passing value must also meet to be shown ok; a value that meets 'healthy' and fails this is warn, shown in amber and never a matter (FS-021-monitors.3.3, FS-021-monitors.3.7). It narrows whichever 'healthy' applies, and a warn with none to narrow is a declaration error (FS-021-monitors.3.5).

from.description: Where the value comes from (FS-021-monitors.5), taken whole from the home that names it.

every.description: How often the monitor is read: a floor between reads, not a promise (FS-021-monitors.6.1, FS-021-monitors.6.5). Defaults to '10m', or to '1d' where 'at' is stated and '1w' where that 'at' names a day.

at.description: Pins the slots to the local clock: 'HH:MM', or 'Mon 06:00' with an 'every' of whole weeks (FS-021-monitors.6.1); null at the site unpins the manifest's (FS-021-monitors.6.2).

timeout.description: Seconds a command may run before it is stopped and the read is unreadable. Defaults to 30 (FS-021-monitors.5.5).

drop_after.description: Failing readings in a row that make the monitor down. Defaults to 1 (FS-021-monitors.10.1).

recover_after.description: Passing readings in a row that end a drop. Defaults to 2 under an hourly interval and to 1 at an hour or longer (FS-021-monitors.10.1).

workflow.description: A runtime workflow proposed for the monitor's drop: it heads the drop's menu, ahead even of what ephor itself recognized (FS-021-monitors.16.1). One choice with 'action', and the site's choice replaces the manifest's whole.

action.description: The id of a menu entry that hands work over, a recipe or a workflow, proposed for the monitor's drop in place of a workflow; one that names no such entry is passed over (FS-021-monitors.16.1).

monitorId.description: A monitor's id, unique within its project; across the site the monitor is '<project>/<id>' (FS-021-monitors.1.1).

monitorCondition.description: A condition on the value (FS-021-monitors.3.1): 'is' for a boolean; 'min' and 'max', inclusive, for a number or a series; 'in' or 'at_most' for a level. A value meets it when it meets every key it holds. A key that does not fit the monitor's kind, or a condition no value can meet, is that monitor's declaration error (FS-021-monitors.4.6).

monitorFrom.description: Where the value comes from (FS-021-monitors.5): a command, run as a summons once per read however many monitors name it (FS-021-monitors.5.1), or a file in the answer shape, read and never run (FS-021-monitors.5.2). Both resolve in the project's checkout of its default branch, or the forest repository 'cwd' names (FS-021-monitors.5.3). Absent, the monitor is read from the answer that brings its samples (FS-021-monitors.5.6).

monitorDuration.description: A whole number and a unit: m minutes, h hours, d days, w weeks (FS-021-monitors.6.1).

kind.description: 'rhei', 'beads', or another store ephor has a reader for.

command.description: A command line run via sh -c in the resolved place (FS-006-project-interface.3).

feature.description: One feature a smoke test can run alone. The same shape the answer envelope uses, spelled here too so this schema validates offline (FS-006-project-interface.11).

paths.description: Globs relating the feature to source paths, for change-driven selection.

branch.description: A branch template says where handed-over work belongs (FS-005-dispatch.25); an offer that runs a command runs in the workspace the project already has.

root.description: A root template places handed-over work (FS-005-dispatch.1, FS-005-dispatch.28); an offer that runs a command hands no work over.

autorun.description: Work nobody has to start is said on the thing that hands work over (FS-005-dispatch.28); an offer that runs a command here has no run to start.

offer.description: One menu entry the project offers. It either runs a command here or lays down one of the runtime's workflows — never both and never neither (FS-006-project-interface.9, FS-005-dispatch.19).

workflow.description: The id of a workflow the bound runtime offers (FS-005-dispatch.19). What it lays down is a plan of its own beside the matter's, and it is offered where the workflow can be filled in.

inputs.description: What this entry answers the workflow's inputs with (FS-005-dispatch.19). A string is rendered with the matter's fields where it names them — {branch}, {repo}, {number}, {title}, {url}, {workspace}, {root}, plus {dossier} and {item} for the files ephor writes; anything else is passed on as it stands.

hands.description: Inputs of that workflow that name who does the work, for a workflow whose own manifest does not say so. Each resolves through ephor's hand resolution and is refused where a narrowing does not permit it (DA-006-hands-fill-a-workflows-targets).

branch.description: Which branch the work this offer lays down belongs on, where the matter has none of its own (FS-005-dispatch.25). A template rendered from the matter's fields as `inputs` are — 'fix/issue-{number}' — and never naming {branch}, {workspace} or {reply}, which are what it produces. Saying it means the work needs the checkout, and the dispatch makes that branch's workspace under the registry's own branch_root_template. Only on an offer that names a workflow.

root.description: The whole work-root template for the workflow this offer lays down (FS-005-dispatch.1, FS-005-dispatch.28). Rendered after branch placement with the same matter values as project placement; only on an offer that names a workflow.

autorun.description: The work this offer lays down needs nobody to start it (FS-005-dispatch.28): `ephor work dispatch` lays it about a matching matter that no recipe covers and that has no work, and the sweep that follows starts what it laid. Omitted is today's behaviour — the entry is a menu row the reader lays and the reader starts. Only on an offer that names a workflow.

requires.description: Capability rungs this offer needs (FS-006-project-interface.10); unmet rungs render '(unavailable: …)'. 'ticketed' and 'local-issues' are older spellings of 'tasks' and still resolve.

background.description: Run beneath the interface as a job rather than taking the terminal (FS-005-dispatch.17). Default false: an offer may be a pager or an editor.

window.description: Run in a window of the reader's own where one is bound, instead of taking the terminal (FS-005-dispatch.22). For the offer that is a program somebody types into — an editor, a pager, a coding agent's own session. Never with `background`: those are two different places.

selector.description: The shared offer/recipe selector language (FS-006-project-interface.9): the same fields a work recipe's 'when' takes, so one language selects both. Every stated field must hold; a field left out asks nothing.

kinds.description: Item kinds as ephor spells them; 'message' is accepted for 'msg'.

awaits.description: Why the matter waits on the reader, any one of them (FS-005-dispatch.31.2): 'conversation' — its conversation awaits the reader; 'unclaimed' — it is an issue nobody holds, on a source that counts that as waiting. A matter that does not wait answers neither; one that waits and records no reason waits on its conversation.

items.description: An entry names something: `login` or `!login`. A field that asks for nothing is written by omitting the field (FS-005-dispatch.31).

assignees.description: Logins the matter must be held by — any one of them — and '!login' one it must not be held by at all (FS-005-dispatch.31). A matter whose source reported nothing about assignment answers neither form and is refused.

items.description: An entry names something: `label` or `!label`. A field that asks for nothing is written by omitting the field (FS-005-dispatch.31).

labels.description: Labels the matter must carry — any one of them — and '!label' one it must not carry at all (FS-005-dispatch.31). A matter whose source reported nothing about labels answers neither form and is refused.

meta.description: What the matter's own source said about this matter, asked as a map because each key is a different question (FS-005-dispatch.31.1). Every key must hold, and each is compared as a string, so "tier": "1" matches a tier the source wrote as a bare 1. A matter whose source reported nothing, or one reporting no such key, is refused rather than matched. There is no '!' form.

behind.description: The matter's branch trails its main branch (true) or is level with it (false), measured in the checkout. An unmeasurable checkout matches neither (FS-004-quick-actions.6).

behind_upstream.description: The matter's branch trails its own published copy (true) or is level with it (false), measured in the checkout. A branch published nowhere matches neither (FS-004-quick-actions.8).
